page: UpCloud 80xCPU-512GB is a general-purpose server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7543 processor with 80 physical cores and 80 vCPUs, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.4 GB of RAM per core, alongside a bundled 2048 GB local SSD storage volume and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU encryption and physics tests all ranking in the top 10%. Single-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth is also highly capable, with cached small-block reads reaching 5364.31 GB/sec and uncached large-block writes at 112.07 GB/sec.

Despite the high core count and massive memory capacity, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained, co-located workloads. Additionally, while the server excels in multi-threaded CPU tasks, its single-threaded performance and certain memory-bound operations, such as the PassMark memory score, fall into the average tier. LLM text generation performance is a notable bottleneck, with medium-model generation scoring in the bottom 25%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density, combining substantial compute and memory on a single instance without the premium cost of dedicated-core bare metal.

This server is well-suited for highly parallelized workloads, including multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput Redis caching. It is also appropriate for large-scale web serving and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a balance of high memory capacity and multi-core processing.
